reason: This passage is a royal and political chronicle narrating events from the perspective of official history-keeping and state authority. It focuses exclusively on the actions of kings (Zedekiah, Nebuchadnezzar), military commanders (Nebuzaradan), and political officials (Gedaliah). While the text mentions 'the people of the land' (עַם הָאָרֶץ), they appear only as objects of actions taken by those in power—being deported, starving during siege, or fleeing—not as the viewpoint through which events are interpreted. The narrative concerns royal lineage, military campaigns, political decisions, and the fate of the elite classes, entirely absent of any perspective from ordinary workers or common people.
